title: Impact of cosmic evolution on the gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic strings
abstract: In the standard cosmological paradigm, the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from a cosmic string network is well defined. However, early-Universe dynamics can significantly alter this relic signal. We systematically investigate how different new physics epochs in the radiation era--including extra relativistic degrees of freedom, early matter domination, intermediate vacuum domination, and kination--modify string network evolution and loop production. We find that a kination era enhances the stochastic GW signal, whereas the other scenarios suppress the signal to varying degrees. We also demonstrate that late-time dynamical dark energy has a negligible impact on the GW spectrum from cosmic strings.

title: In situ enhanced detectability of axions' responses in a microwave cavity
abstract: Microwave cavities in strong magnetic fields are among the most sensitive detectors for axion dark matter detection. Its sensitivity, however, is fundamentally limited by the second order nature of axion photon energy conversion, which yields an extremely weak signal. Here we propose a feasible approach to break this limitation, by pre-exciting the target cavity mode to generate a first order power response signal in situ. The resulting signal amplitude scales linearly with the axion-photon coupling parameter, which is in sharp contrast to the quadratic scaling of conventional schemes, and is detectable via standard quadrature balanced homodyne detection system, even though its phase remains stochastic. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this pre-excited seed field can effectively suppress thermal noise, and thus the detection sensitivity of the system can approach the lower quantum noise limit. Consequently, the sensitivities predicted by the KSVZ and DFSZ models could be surpassed. This proposal might offer a pathway to a major leap in axion dark matter searches, as it is within reach of current technology.

title: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
abstract: We present FeynFacet, a workflow in which artificial intelligence agents develop and execute programs for analytic next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculations, with the observables and conventions specified by physicists. We use it to derive new analytic hard functions for single-inclusive transverse spin transfer in proton-proton and lepton-proton collisions. The new proton-proton results cover all partonic channels contributing to transverse spin transfer, and the new lepton-proton result is inclusive in the scattered lepton. Within FeynFacet, we use reverse unitarity to represent the on-shell delta functions in real-emission phase-space integrals as cut propagators. Dimensional shifts convert integrals containing evanescent numerators into scalar integrals in higher dimensions. Integration-by-parts identities then reduce the scalar integrals to master integrals, which are evaluated analytically. Gauge invariance, pole cancellation and renormalization-group (RG) evolution provide checks throughout the calculation. We reproduce established single-inclusive hard functions for unpolarized and double longitudinally polarized proton-proton and lepton-proton scattering, and for proton-proton scattering with two transversely polarized beams. We also reproduce the NLO matching coefficients for unpolarized quark and gluon transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions and the associated soft functions. The new transverse spin-transfer coefficients provide perturbative inputs for extracting quark transversity through spin-dependent fragmentation, including polarized-hyperon production, Collins and dihadron asymmetries in jets, and spin-dependent one- and two-point energy correlators. We make all analytic coefficients and the associated calculation programs publicly available online.

title: Soft scalar-field corrections to the topological susceptibility
abstract: We compute the contribution from soft scalar-field fluctuations to the topological susceptibility in SU(2) gauge theory at high temperature. We construct a 3-dimensional effective theory for the scalar field that accounts for the presence of an instanton. In the limit that the scalar selfcoupling $ \lambda $ is much larger than the square of the gauge coupling $g$ we obtain a correction of order $\sqrt{\lambda}$ relative to the 1-loop result for the topological susceptibility.

title: Discontinuity at the Pole
abstract: The exchange of a particle whose mass is taken to zero need not reproduce the exchange of a particle that is strictly massless from the outset. We derive a general on-shell diagnostic of the well-known discontinuity between the exchange of a massless particle and the massless limit of a massive-particle exchange, valid for a mediator of arbitrary integer spin S. Our main observation is that this discontinuity can be identified directly at the level of the pole residue. We find that, in four dimensions, the residue is governed by a Chebyshev polynomial in the massless case and by a Legendre polynomial in the massless limit of the massive case. For S = 2, this reproduces the van Dam-Veltman-Zakharov discontinuity. For general S, it provides a simple and compact higher-spin analogue from on-shell factorisation. The discontinuity is probed, in principle, by the leading post-Newtonian correction to the non-relativistic potential between two massive scalar bodies.

title: Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the Cosmic Microwave Background
abstract: Topological defects are a generic prediction of field theories with spontaneously broken symmetries, and domain walls, the two-dimensional defects left by a broken discrete symmetry, are among the simplest. We study the imprint of dark, purely gravitationally interacting domain walls on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in the regime where a low symmetry-breaking scale $\eta$ allows the walls to evade the Zel'dovich overclosure bound while remaining cosmologically relevant. The relativistic repulsion of matter by a planar wall carves out an evacuated void bounded by an overdense shell, and we compute the resulting photon deflection field analytically for walls both aligned with and arbitrarily inclined to the line of sight. The deflection stamps coherent, strongly non-Gaussian distortions onto the temperature sky, with a characteristic two-peak structure set by the relativistic displacement scale and an inclination dependence that vanishes for face-on walls. Because these signatures are localised and anisotropic, they are poorly captured by two-point statistics; we therefore analyse them with a curvelet/wavelet decomposition matched to the wall's geometry, and with simulation-based inference, training a Neural Posterior Estimator (NPE) to recover the scattering redshift $z$, energy scale $\eta$, and inclination $\theta$, and a Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) to evaluate the likelihood-ratio test statistic for limit-setting. Casting these methods as sensitivity forecasts for a South Pole Telescope-like (SPT) survey, we find that the curvelet and wavelet statistical thresholds populate a common $\eta \sim 10-100$ MeV band over the accessible redshift range. The neural-ratio sensitivity curve, which exploits the full map morphology, reaches a factor 1.3-1.9 lower in $\eta$ at $z \gtrsim 20$, or $\sim 2-7$ in the wall tension, landing essentially on the per-resolution-element noise floor.

title: Flavored $S_{3}$ Non-Minimal Left-Right Symmetric Model
abstract: In this work we investigate fermion masses and flavor mixings in a non-minimal left-right symmetric model endowed with the non-Abelian discrete symmetry $S_3$. The scalar sector contains three Higgs bidoublets, while one left-handed and one right-handed triplet generate Majorana neutrino masses. Assigning the first two fermion families to an $S_3$ doublet and the third family to a singlet, together with a specific alignment of the bidoublet vacuum expectation values, leads to a common and analytically tractable structure for the fermion mass matrices. We study both the pseudomanifest and manifest left-right realizations, in which the fermion mass matrices are complex symmetric and Hermitian, respectively, and derive analytical expressions for the left- and right-handed CKM and PMNS mixing matrices. A numerical likelihood test shows that the model successfully reproduces the observed quark and lepton mixing patterns for both normal and inverted neutrino mass orderings at the level of oscillation data. Remarkably, the manifest scenario emerges as a more restrictive realization of the pseudomanifest one, with the main distinction residing in their CP-phase structure. We further explore the phenomenological consequences for the neutrinoless double-beta decay, the muon anomalous magnetic moment, and the lepton-flavor-violating decay $\mu\to e\gamma$. The right-handed contribution exhibits the characteristic dependence on the heavy-neutrino and $W_R$ mass scales, while flavor corrections are found to be subleading over most of the allowed parameter space. These results show that an $S_3$ flavor symmetry can simultaneously organize fermion mixing and lead to distinctive low-energy signatures within left-right symmetric theories.

title: Measurements of the neutron background for the Colorado Underground Research Institute (CURIE)
abstract: We present the first direct measurements of the neutron background at the Colorado Underground Research Institute (CURIE), a shallow-underground facility with an effective overburden of approximately $400$~m.w.e.\ in the Edgar Experimental Mine in Idaho Springs, Colorado. The radiogenic and muon-induced components were characterized in the Subatomic Particle Hideout. The radiogenic component was measured with a custom Bonner Cylinder Spectrometer comprising a $^{3}$He proportional counter and six cylindrical high-density polyethylene moderators. Its response functions were simulated in \textsc{geant4}, empirically calibrated using a $^{239}$Pu-$^{9}$Be source and the shadow-cone method, and then corrected to account for the approximately isotropic underground field. Unfolding the measured count rates gives a total local scalar neutron flux, dominated by radiogenic production, for $E_n\lesssim\SI{10}{\MeV}$ of $(2.51\pm0.58_{\rm stat}\pm0.39_{\rm sys})\times10^{-5}$~\si{\per\square\centi\meter\per\second}. The muon-induced component was measured with a BC-501A organic liquid scintillator operated for \SI{1431}{\hour}. Pulse shape discrimination identified 55~$\pm$~7 neutron candidates. Using the simulated detector response, these counts yield an integral muon-induced neutron flux at the rock--cavern boundary above \SI{10.5}{\MeV} of $(2.09\pm0.29_{\rm stat}\,{}^{+0.79}_{-0.53}{}_{\rm sys})\times10^{-7}$~\si{\per\square\centi\meter\per\second}. This flux uses the first-entry, boundary-area normalization of a previous CURIE simulation study. Its central value is approximately \SI{12}{\percent} higher than the site-specific prediction but is consistent within the reported uncertainties. Together, these measurements characterize the radiogenic and high-energy cosmogenic neutron environments at CURIE and provide quantitative input for planning future low-background experiments at the facility.

title: A localisation bound for Standard-Model representations in heterotic orbifolds
abstract: In heterotic string compactifications on toroidal orbifolds, the massless states at a twisted fixed point are constrained by the evenness of the sixteen-dimensional gauge lattice. We show that two massless left-chiral states in the same Standard-Model representation, built on the same constructing space-group element and distinct modulo the Weyl group of $SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L$, must satisfy $\sqrt{R}+\sqrt{R'}\ge\sqrt{2}$, where $R$ is the squared length of the part of a state's gauge momentum orthogonal to the Standard-Model Cartan directions. Without left-moving oscillator excitations this reads $R\ge 1/2$. When $R<1$, $n$ such states, pairwise distinct in the same sense, carry the weights of the fundamental representation of a local $SU(n)$ commuting with the Standard Model, and $n\le 1/(1-R)$. Since the representation fixes the projected length (at the canonical hypercharge normalisation, $6/5$ for the 10-like $Q$, $u^c$, $e^c$ and $4/5$ for the 5bar-like $d^c$ and lepton doublet), the bound becomes a condition on the sector: a repeated 10-like representation requires a massless budget of at least $17/20$, a repeated 5bar-like one at least $13/20$. In the complete massless spectra of 16,138 models from two orbifold catalogues the multiplicity ceiling is reached at four values of $R$. We exhibit an explicit model on $T^6/(Z_3\times Z_6)$ whose budget clears the higher threshold and carries a repeated 10-like representation at the multiplicity the bound permits. For the Standard Model embedded through $SU(5)$ in one $E_8$ factor we show that, for that geometry and budget, exactly two inequivalent order-six shift classes admit such a doubling, and among the embeddings over them with the Standard Model intact we find none with three net generations of $Q$, $u^c$ and $e^c$ at once.

title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is sensitive to the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos, providing a probe of gravothermal evolution in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). We combine semi-analytic cold dark matter (CDM) subhalo histories with a model for gravothermal evolution in SIDM to generate CDM and SIDM subhalo populations across SIDM parameter space. We predict their projected enclosed masses and deflection-based projected density slopes and compare them with three perturbers inferred through gravitational imaging in PJ011646, SDSS J0946+1006, and JVAS B1938+666. For SIDM model parameters $\sigma_0/m_\chi=147.1$ cm$^2$/g and $w=120$ km/s, SIDM subhalos reproduce all three perturbers more often than CDM subhalos. For PJ011646, we find ~0.6 cored SIDM subhalos per host matching the perturber, compared with ~0.002 in CDM, while core-collapsed subhalos are too steep. For SDSS J0946+1006, we find ~3 core-collapsed and ~0.004 cored SIDM subhalos per host, compared with none in 900 CDM realizations, although baryons, neglected here, may matter for such massive subhalos. For "detection V" in JVAS B1938+666, we find ~220 core-collapsed and ~20 cored SIDM subhalos per host within the $2\sigma$ posterior region, compared with ~0.2 in CDM; the CDM candidates require exceptionally early accretion, at median redshift $z\sim13$. Simultaneously reproducing all three perturbers requires $w\gtrsim10^2$ km/s, so that the massive (~$5.6\times10^{10}M_\odot$) progenitors of SDSS J0946+1006 candidates can collapse, and is achieved for $\sigma_0/m_\chi\gtrsim10^2$ cm$^2$/g in the parameter sets studied. Our results show how semi-analytic models can quantify how often subhalos reproduce individual perturbers in different dark matter models, and our modular framework can be readily updated as models of tidal stripping and late-stage gravothermal evolution in SIDM improve. (abridged)

title: Magnetic field effect on neutral color superconductivity as a mechanism to boost the inner magnetic field of magnetars
abstract: In this paper, we review the impact of a strong magnetic field on the neutral two-flavor color superconducting (2SC) phase of dense quark matter. Using a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model approach in the mean-field approximation, we first solve the gap equations for the diquark condensate $\Delta$ and the electric chemical potential $\mu_e$ under a uniform external magnetic field, and discuss the coupled evolution of the chiral and diquark order parameters. We then evaluate the field-dependent Meissner masses of the rotationally charged gluons for a wide range of densities and moderate diquark coupling strengths. Combining the "zero-mode problem" mechanism with the neutrality condition, we show that the gluon masses become tachyonic even at moderate magnetic-field values, signaling a chromomagnetic instability in density regions where the system was stable at zero field. This instability can be resolved through the restructuring of the ground state with the formation of a gluon vortex condensate. A remarkable consequence of the vortex configuration is the paramagnetic amplification of the in-medium magnetic field: seed fields of the order of $10^{15}$ G can be enhanced by up to two orders of magnitude, reaching $\sim 10^{17}$ G, precisely the range predicted for magnetar cores. We compare this microscopic mechanism with the conventional dynamo explanation and discuss how it offers a plausible explanation for the extremely high magnetic fields expected to be realized in magnetar interiors.

title: Prediction of the Geoneutrino Signal at the Jinping Neutrino Experiment
abstract: We present refined predictions of the geoneutrino flux for the 500-tonne Jinping Neutrino Experiment (JNE). We construct a local crustal model with a resolution of \(0.2^\circ\times0.2^\circ\) based on the SWChinaCVM-2.0 seismic velocity model and integrate it with CRUST1.0 to establish our reference model. For comparison, we also calculate the geoneutrino flux using ECM1 and CRUST1.0 as standalone global crustal models. Assuming an energy scale of 500~p.e./MeV and an exposure of 500~t$\times$1500~days, we predict the inverse beta decay event spectrum, including both the geoneutrino signal and the reactor antineutrino background. The distinct spectral shapes of the $^{238}$U, $^{232}$Th, and reactor antineutrino components allow their respective contributions to be obtained through spectral fitting. These predictions provide inputs for the JNE data analysis, particularly for extracting the mantle geoneutrino signal and testing competing bulk silicate Earth models.

title: Coherent axion electrodynamics in OSIRIS: a counter-propagating axion-photon parametric instability
abstract: We present a coherent axion-electrodynamics extension of the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code and use it to identify and benchmark a parametric axion-photon instability supported by two equal counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps. The module evolves a cell-centered axion field together with a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response on the native staggered OSIRIS grid. Re-examining the previously proposed strictly co-linear branch shows that it is removed when the axion-Maxwell equations are reduced consistently. A closely related standing-wave geometry, however, supports a distinct Floquet instability. We derive the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair and obtain a reduced analytic growth rate and cutoff for the dominant long-wavelength envelope branch. For an axion mass-to-pump-frequency ratio of 0.06 and a per-beam vector-potential amplitude of 0.3, simulations at coupling strengths of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 reproduce both the growth-rate spectrum and the coupling-dependent instability boundary. The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80, and 13.23, while OSIRIS finds exponential growth through modes 8, 10, and 13, respectively, with the next resolved modes stable. The electromagnetic diagnostics additionally resolve exponentially growing sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber, while the zero-wavenumber electric component exhibits no sustained growth, as expected for the unstable Floquet eigenvector. The agreement provides an end-to-end benchmark of the coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling and demonstrates that parametric growth of the axion field is present in a two-beam pump geometry.

title: Coupled-channel extension of the effective-range expansion with left-hand cut
abstract: We generalize the recently proposed effective-range expansion with a left-hand cut [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 011903 (2025)] to a coupled-channel framework. By systematically analyzing the singularity structure of the $S$-wave coupled-channel one-particle exchange (OPE) potential under various mass configurations, we derive an analytical parametrization of the coupled-channel scattering amplitude that incorporates the OPE left-hand cut for multiple channels. Taking the two-channel case as an illustration, we benchmark this parametrization against the Lippmann--Schwinger equation (LSE) by comparing the amplitudes and their inverses at different expansion orders. Even at the lowest order, with only six parameters, the coupled-channel parametrization faithfully reproduces the LSE results and enables precise extraction of the coupling constants, demonstrating its reliability for two-body coupled-channel scattering problems involving particle exchange.

title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(\tau_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(\mu_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.

title: Higher-twist hadronic tensor in deep inelastic scattering with massive quarks
abstract: In this paper, we calculate the inclusive deep inelastic scattering (DIS) with finite quark masses up to twist-4 accuracy based on collinear expansion method. The collinear expansion method not only naturally leads to gauge-invariant correlation functions and parton distribution functions, but also yields a remarkably compact expression for the hadronic tensor. The resulting hadronic tensor can be organized according to the corresponding power behavior in $1/Q$. In particular, the explicit quark-mass dependence gives rise to additional power-suppressed contributions and the ratio $m/Q$ can be counted as a twist-3 contribution in the power expansion. As an application, we further investigate the role of transversity in inclusive DIS with a transversely polarized target. We find that the transversity distribution appears explicitly in the quark-quark correlation function and gives rise to a contribution proportional to $m~h_{1T}/Q$. However, this contribution is exactly cancelled in the hadronic tensor by the one arising from the corresponding quark-gluon-quark correlation function. This cancellation shows that, within the one-photon-exchange approximation, the mass-induced transversity term cancels in the complete twist-3 hadronic tensor, and no net transversity contribution remains at twist-3 accuracy in inclusive DIS. We complement this analytical study with numerical estimates of the $g_T$-related twist-3 asymmetry, comparing predictions with and without the mass-dependent $x\rightarrow\chi$ rescaling at the same measured $x$. The results show that these kinematic mass effects become more important at lower $Q^2$ and larger $x$.

title: Analytic two-loop corrections to top-quark pair production at hadron colliders
abstract: We present the complete two-loop QCD amplitudes for the production of a top-quark pair in the quark--antiquark annihilation and gluon-fusion channels in analytic form up to order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$. Our analysis maintains full dependence on the top-quark mass and on the number of colours. The amplitudes are expressed in terms of 417 master integrals, which we compute by means of differential equations in $\varepsilon$-factorised form. Their calculation involves several elliptic curves and a hyperelliptic curve of genus two, which makes top-quark pair production an ideal arena for recent methods to construct canonical bases beyond polylogarithms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first scattering amplitude in which iterated integrals related to a genus-two surface survive in the finite remainder in four space-time dimensions. We provide high-precision series expansions at the threshold and combine them with the numerical solution of the differential equations in a code that evaluates the UV-renormalised infrared-finite remainders at arbitrary points of the physical phase space.

title: Gauge-field energy density in inflationary kinetic-coupling models: QFT regularization versus horizon cutoffs
abstract: Coupling gauge fields to the inflaton can amplify their quantum fluctuations during inflation, with potential applications to a range of cosmological phenomena. A central challenge is to define finite and physically meaningful observables, such as the gauge-field energy density. In this work, we study an Abelian gauge field kinetically coupled to the inflaton through $f^2(\phi)F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ in a de Sitter background with $f\propto a^{\gamma_1}$, and compare conventional quantum-field-theoretic regularization with horizon-cutoff prescriptions. Using a hard physical-momentum cutoff and dimensional regularization, we derive the ultraviolet divergences in closed form and fix the remaining one-parameter finite-part ambiguity by requiring the coupling-induced total energy density to be nonnegative. We then examine five horizon-cutoff prescriptions based on characteristic scales of the mode equations. Their predictions depend sensitively on the choice of horizon scale and, for weak gauge-field production, can deviate substantially from the regularized result; for the adopted finite-part prescription, the minimal horizon agrees best with the regularized total energy density. As $|\gamma_1|\to 2$, where infrared modes dominate, the relative deviation of all prescriptions from the regularized result vanishes, independently of the finite-part prescription. Outside this regime, the separate electric and magnetic contributions, which can become negative after regularization, are not reliably reproduced by any of the horizon-cutoff prescriptions.

title: Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Simulation Using GENIE Event Generator
authors: L. F. B. M. Rodrigues (Federal University of Alfenas
F. G. Gardim (Federal University of Alfenas
G. A. Valdiviesso (Federal University of Alfenas
abstract: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) relies on the precise reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to extract oscillation parameters. The use of Liquid Argon introduces significant theoretical complexities due to nuclear effects. This work evaluates neutrino-nucleus scattering models using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. We demonstrate the limitations of the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model in the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel and its reliance on an inflated Axial Mass to match experimental data from MicroBooNE. We show that transitioning to advanced many-body frameworks, specifically the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) supplemented with Random Phase Approximation (RPA), is needed. Additionally, we evaluate the impact of the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates on Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), concluding that modernized constraints are a prerequisite for mitigating systematic biases in DUNE.

title: Systematic Study of Neutrino-Nucleus Interactions for the DUNE Experiment
authors: L. F. B. M. Rodrigues (Federal University of Alfenas
F. G. Gardim (Federal University of Alfenas
G. A. Valdiviesso (Federal University of Alfenas
abstract: The recent generation of high-precision neutrino oscillation experiments, such as the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), relies on the accurate reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to determine fundamental parameters like Charge-Parity (CP) violation and the neutrino mass hierarchy. The use of Liquid Argon, introduces significant theoretical complexities. This dissertation provides a investigation into neutrino-nucleus scattering phenomenologies, connecting fundamental electroweak theory with computational simulations using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. The study evaluates the limitations of traditional frameworks, such as the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model, specifically addressing the Axial Mass parameter and its impact on the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel. By comparing baseline RFG predictions against experimental data from MicroBooNE, this research quantifies the necessity of advanced many-body nuclear frameworks. The implementation of the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) model, Random Phase Approximation (RPA) screening, and the SuperScaling Approximation (SuSAv2) are systematically analyzed to resolve kinematic biases. Additionally, the impact of modernized phenomenological constraints, including the updated $M_A^{RES} = 0.96$ GeV for resonant pion production and the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates for Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), is evaluated. Furthermore, this research integrates university extension initiatives by developing and presenting macroscopic 3D-printed educational models, consisting of a Linear Accelerator (LINAC) analog and a scattering experiment, and finally presenting it into the festival "Mais Ci\^encia Por Favor".

title: A universal probe of QCD spin physics from fragmentation energy correlator
abstract: We study the fragmentation energy correlator (FEC), which combines the nonperturbative fragmentation function with the infrared-safe energy correlator, as a new probe of the three-dimensional dynamics of QCD hadronization. We demonstrate, both theoretically and numerically, that FEC applies universally to inclusive hadron production in lepton-lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions, without requiring jet algorithms or simultaneous measurements of other heavy objects. Through the nontrivial transverse-spin dependence, FEC provides a sensitive probe of the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale in QCD via its variation with the energy-correlator scale.

title: Timelike Compton scattering on a deuteron target
abstract: We investigate timelike Compton scattering (TCS) on a deuteron target as a probe of the three-dimensional partonic structure of the deuteron encoded in generalized parton distributions (GPDs). Such measurements may provide new insight into the internal structure of the deuteron, and help to clarify the unresolved tensor-polarization puzzle. We present numerical estimates of the leading-order (in the strong coupling $\alpha_s$) TCS cross section in the kinematic region relevant to future measurements at Jefferson Lab. The deuteron GPDs are evaluated within a convolution model, while the Bethe-Heitler contribution is calculated using a phenomenological parametrization of the deuteron electromagnetic form factors. In addition, we derive the theoretical expressions for the next-to-leading-order corrections to deuteron TCS, with particular emphasis on contributions from the gluon transversity GPDs. We show that these contributions can be isolated through their characteristic angular dependence in the center-of-mass frame of the produced lepton pair. Our results demonstrate the potential of deuteron TCS as a complementary probe of both the quark and gluon structure of the deuteron at Jefferson Lab.

title: Heavy Sterile Fermions from the Atmosphere: LZ Limits on Neutrino Up-Scattering
abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has recently reported data extending to nuclear-recoil energies of about 270 keV, including a single event at 248 keV in a nearly background-free region, for an exposure of 2.84 tonne-years. We examine this dataset through neutrino up-scattering to a heavy sterile fermion induced by atmospheric neutrinos, mediated by vector, axial-vector, scalar and dipole interactions. Our main result is a set of constraints: using the part of the LZ data where no excess is observed, we obtain new bounds on all four scenarios that probe regions of parameter space not tested before, and show that dark matter detectors can provide competitive limits on neutrino up-scattering for sterile fermion masses above $\sim 50$ MeV. We also test whether the 248~keV event can be explained in this way while remaining consistent with the absence of events at lower recoil energies. For the scalar, vector and axial mediators this requires couplings at the edge of perturbativity, while the dipole does not provide a good fit, so we conclude that up-scattering is not a compelling explanation of the event.

title: Robustness of the scaled transverse-momentum correlator and the contribution of meson--baryon fluctuations at RHIC energies
abstract: The search for the QCD critical point relies on identifying non-monotonic signatures in event-by-event fluctuation observables, such as the scaled two-particle transverse-momentum correlator $C_{p_T}$. Using a microscopic transport model (UrQMD), we establish the robustness of $C_{p_T}$ against the variations that distinguish the datasets in the relevant collision energy regime, namely the choice of centrality estimator, finite tracking efficiency, and acceptance, including the difference between collider and fixed-target running. In addition, it has recently been proposed, based on UrQMD yields, that the measured non-monotonicity requires no critical dynamics and instead follows from the event-by-event composition of the final state. We show that this contribution is governed by event-by-event fluctuations in the meson-baryon composition, rather than by the mean yields alone. Using the composition fluctuations obtained from UrQMD, we find that the minimum in the two-component calculation disappears.

title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
abstract: The origin of the excess of GeV gamma-rays in the Milky Way's galactic center observed by Fermi-LAT has been an open question for nearly two decades. The two leading interpretations of this signal are that it is produced either by annihilating dark matter (DM), or arises from unresolved point sources, such as a novel population of millisecond pulsars. In both scenarios, uncertainties and limitations in the modeling of galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, such as the steady-state approximation of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and assumption of an axisymmetric distribution of CRs, complicate the interpretation of the galactic center excess (GCE). Simulations with full magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and CR transport can provide a new avenue for understanding the astrophysical phenomena that drive galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission. We utilize MHD simulations of Milky Way analogs with time-dependent, spectrally-resolved CR transport to reconstruct diffuse gamma-ray emission. Comparing instantaneous emission to a time-averaged baseline, we find residuals up to several times larger than the Fermi GCE, with a wide range of spectral shapes and spatial morphologies. At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.

title: Radiation damage and recovery of SiPMs exposed to low-momentum muon beams for innovative scintillation-based muon beam monitors
abstract: Silicon PhotoMultipliers (SiPMs) are among the standard devices for light detection in scintillator detectors. Some detector designs require these devices to be placed in radioactive areas or directly exposed to particle beams. Specifically, the damage from exposure to low-momentum muons is particularly important, as they have a high energy deposit and they have several applications in material science and particle physics. Eight SiPM models from different manufacturers were exposed to 29 MeV/c positive muons, with an intensity of O(10^6) muons/s for 13 hours, maximising the charge deposited in the depletion region. I-V curves were measured before/after irradiation and annealing; DCR and crosstalk analyses are ongoing, to extract dark count rate and optical crosstalk. Despite showing a measurable increase in dark current, the devices preserved operational stability. Thermal annealing has also been tested by heating the devices at 125{\deg}C, showing a recovery of the optimal SiPM features. This work is part of a collaboration between the University of Pavia and ISIS, to develop detectors for low-momentum muons (< 40 MeV/c), based on thin scintillators.

title: The scintillating fibre beam monitor for the CHNet-MAXI experiment at ISIS: characterisation of the light collection and detection system
abstract: The CHNet-MAXI experiment at ISIS aims at a non-destructive isotopic characterisation of lead samples, based on muonic atom formation. A custom scintillation-based detector is used for the reconstruction of the time and space distributions of the low-energy muon beam employed in the experiment. The beam monitor consists of two orthogonal planes of 10 cm-long, 3 mm $\times$ 3 mm square scintillating fibres, totalling 64 fibres, read out by four arrays of 16 Hamamatsu S14160-3015PS SiPMs each. The optical performance of the detector has been characterised, focusing on the SiPM behaviour, and also checking and correcting the uniformity of the light response across channels with a $^{60}$ Co source. A first detector test with protons at the CNAO-XPR has been carried out. The results of the Geant4 simulation of the detector, fundamental for the detector operation and data analysis, are also presented. All these activities are preliminary to the final detector operation in the CHNet-MAXI experiment at the RIKEN-RAL Port4 decay muon beamline at ISIS.

title: Fermion Scattering on Quantum Computers
abstract: Resonant scattering links particle interactions to the formation and decay of unstable excitations. We develop a hybrid quantum-computing framework to study these dynamics through fermion--antifermion collisions. Our formulation of $(1+1)$-dimensional Yukawa theory encodes fermions in qubits and the scalar field in qumodes. We identify the operations needed for a photonic implementation and benchmark the dynamics with tensor-network simulations. Near resonance, we resolve the build-up of a localised scalar excitation and the subsequent partial return of energy to the fermions. Enhanced entanglement accompanies this exchange. Time-dependent correlator measurements reproduce the analytically predicted decay rate to a few percent precision, with energy scans exhibiting a resonance peak consistent with packet-averaged Breit--Wigner behaviour. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

title: The renormalization of the shell-model neutrinoless double-beta decay operator starting from effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order
abstract: This paper is the continuation of a previous study, where shell-model calculations of the matrix elements for the neutrinoless double-beta decay were performed within a fully-consistent framework, starting from expressions of the nuclear Hamiltonian and decay operators which have been derived through chiral perturbation theory. The decays under our investigation are those involving 48Ca, 76Ge, and 82Se, as in our earlier analyses of electroweak nuclear decays with Hamiltonians and operators derived within effective field theory. In this work we focus on perturbative properties of the chiral expansion of the decay operator, namely in assessing the weight of terms beyond the leading order on the nuclear matrix elements of medium-mass candidates. To this end, we have constructed effective shell-model decay operators starting from two-body currents up to next-to-next-to-leading order and, for the first time, we introduce for nuclei of experimental interest contributions of the three-body current operators, which emerge at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order of the chiral perturbation theory. Our investigation is aimed to evaluate the theoretical uncertainties affecting the calculated nuclear matrix elements of the neutrinoless double-beta decay, by conjugating the estimate of the inaccuracy related to the finiteness of the degrees of freedom of the nuclear model and the truncation of the chiral expansion of the decay operator.
